items.title: Ran Blake interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 16, 2021
items.q: I went home thinking of Barbara and her mother Nellie and the whole family

ctx.x: Thank you for that. That makes me feel a little better. Let me talk about song titles for a moment. Do you write pieces with a song title in mind? Or do you name them halfway through or perhaps when they’re done?

Well rarely do I think of it before. I know I’ve written two pieces in the last year that I wish musicians would cover, “Memphis” for Martin Luther King, Jean Plumez, and “The Short Life of Barbara Monk.” With Barbara Monk I remember getting ready to take off at Logan Airport to get to the funeral and I passed out in Boston and I went home thinking of Barbara and her mother Nellie and the whole family and the cousin Jackie Beneaux, and I wrote for his niece [plays piano]. But in “Memphis” I thought particularly…

Oh that’s very interesting. Some of these thoughts that I have and these questions, I don’t really honestly think they have an answer. Like what does music mean? What can it mean if it’s an abstract art form, especially if there’s no singing? There’s no clear story. So will it affect different people very differently.
